qt: to the Commission Daniel Buda (PPE) Subject:

Rising gas prices and the conflict in the Middle East could affect future fertiliser prices. So far, prices have remained stable due to low demand and cheap imports from Egypt and Russia. All the same, the spread of the conflict in the Middle East could change this situation. Urea prices have recently dropped on the world market due to a tender from Indian, but a gradual increase is expected. Chinese exports of urea have stalled, but supply remains high and demand remains low in Brazil and Europe. Ammonium nitrate prices have also decreased as demand remains low, and Russia is delivering at lower prices. Overall nitrogen demand is currently lower than usual. 1.

Specialists in the field forecast slow but steady growth. In this regard, how does the Commission plan to act to manage potential price increases and ensure stability in the supply of fertilisers in Europe?

Is the Commission ready to take market monitoring measures and pursue strategies to deal with the changes in the Middle East and fluctuations in natural gas prices that could affect the fertiliser industry?
at: (English version) to the Commission Daniel Buda (PPE) (12 January 2024) Subject: Challenge of the rise in fertiliser prices Rising gas prices and the conflict in the Middle East could affect future fertiliser prices. So far, prices have remained stable due to low demand and cheap imports from Egypt and Russia. All the same, the spread of the conflict in the Middle East could change this situation. Urea prices have recently dropped on the world market due to a tender from Indian, but a gradual increase is expected. Chinese exports of urea have stalled, but supply remains high and demand remains low in Brazil and Europe. Ammonium nitrate prices have also decreased as demand remains low, and Russia is delivering at lower prices. Overall nitrogen demand is currently lower than usual. 1. Specialists in the field forecast slow but steady growth. In this regard, how does the Commission plan to act to manage potential price increases and ensure stability in the supply of fertilisers in Europe? 2. Is the Commission ready to take market monitoring measures and pursue strategies to deal with the changes in the Middle East and fluctuations in natural gas prices that could affect the fertiliser industry? (20 February 2024) The Commission monitors the EU fertiliser market developments, in view of possible impact of tensions in the Middle East through, inter alia, the EU Fertilisers Market Observatory (1). The Commission also established a mechanism (2) to improve the degree of preparedness of the EU to handle crises potentially threatening food security in the EU; the possible impact of such tensions was discussed in the framework of that mechanism. The Commission remains committed to pursue the measures to ensure fertilisers availability and affordability listed in its communication on the subject (3). Such measures include among others import diversification of fertilisers, the development of industrial interest in areas such as organic fertilisers produced from recovered residues and by-products or of green and lowcarbon fertilisers productions process, all elements that will make the EU industry less dependent on imports of natural gas. The Commission also closely monitors the fluctuations in natural gas prices and has undertaken a number of measures in the area of energy of supply (4) and diversification of imports (5). As part of these measures, it has launched the EU Energy Platform (6) that among others provides visibility on demand and supply of gas with a calming effect on markets. The Commission maintains a close dialogue with the fertilisers industry in several aspects, including on gas prices, as this industry is among the biggest gas consuming sectors in the Union.
